newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australia, NZ merge aviation markets on Nov 1.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australia, NZ merge aviation markets on Nov 1.

text.p: Australia and New Zealand will merge their aviation markets on November 1, Australian Transport Minister John Sharp and New Zealand Transport Minister Maurice Williamson said on Thursday.

"The new SAM (single aviation market) arrangements mean that airlines of each country gain unrestricted rights to fly anywhere within the other country and have unrestricted rights to fly trans-Tasman services," the ministers said in a joint statement.
Eligible airlines would be subject to these requirements:
--At least 50 percent ownership and effective board control by nationals of Australia, New Zealand or both;
--Two-thirds of the board, including the chairperson, must be Australians, New Zealanders or both;
--A head office and operational base in Australia or New Zealand.

"The ministers further agreed that if News Ltd subsequently sells any of its holding in Ansett New Zealand, then the new owners would need to meet the full (ownership and control) requirements of the SAM text," the ministers said.
"There will be no limit on the number of SAM airlines of either country that can operate services linking any two cities within and directly between the two countries," they said.
Former Australian Labor government's transport minister, Laurie Brereton, cancelled plans for a single aviation market shortly before it was due to come into effect two years ago.
Its impact on the value of Qantas Airways Ltd, then 75 percent government-owned, was given as the reason.
The new Liberal-National government promised before it won the March 2 election to restore the deal.

"The ministers also agreed, following a request from the New Zealand government, to use their discretion under the new arrangements to approve Ansett New Zealand as a SAM carrier," the ministers said.
Air New Zealand, Ansett Australia and Qantas Airways qualified, they said.
Air New Zealand is buying TNT Ltd's 50 percent stake in Ansett's domestic Australian operation.
News Corp, which holds the other 50 percent, will assume full ownership of the New Zealand domestic operator, Ansett New Zealand.

"The SAM arrangements will create a new market worth an estimated A$5 billion and covering more than 31 million passengers a year by bringing together the domestic travel markets of each country, and the trans-Tasman market which links them."
Sharp said he suspected the deal would be reflected in fare prices next year.

Asked if it was reasonable to expect a five percent drop in prices as a result of the agreement, he told reporters: "I'd like to think the figure would be greater, but I would be reluctant to speculate."

The agreement leaves prices unregulated, specifying "no approvals by national aeronautical authorities will be required for tariffs for air transport services between and within Australia and New Zealand."

The Australian federal government has little power over transport regulation internal to any state, and the deal specified that intra-state air services in Australia would still require state government approvals.
